newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares slip in selective, mixed market.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares slip in selective, mixed market.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Wednesday in a mixed market focused on selected paper with dealers foreseeing a rather unclear time ahead.
"I think we are going to see a rather mixed market focussing on selected paper now on top of the recent period of gains," one dealer said.

Sophus Berendsen and Bang & Olufsen were in focus, the former due to rumours of a possible split up with its British Rentokil unit located in a separate company, the latter because of a better than expected first-half 1996/97 result.
The KFX top-20 index lost 0.21 point to close at 144.22.
Sophus closed 11 crowns up at 829 and B & O finished 20 crowns higher at 335.

Tele Danmark attracted attention due to the unveiling of a plan to sack 2,500 staff, ending the day one crown down at 354, while Novo Nordisk put on eight crowns to 558, with more gains seen if as the market expects the strong dollar makes further advances.
Overall bourse turnover was 1.006 billion crowns. The KFX March future fell 1.35 point to 144.15 with 120 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
